newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE coffee holds losses in sluggish trade.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE coffee holds losses in sluggish trade.

text.p: Robusta coffee futures held early losses by the close on Tuesday in sluggish trade dominated by jobbers.
Traders said volume was also far from impressive with just 3,355 lots, mainly switch trades, changing hands.
"The market is probably taking a breather," said one. The market's activity was also curtailed as funds and specs shifted from coffee, once the hot soft-commodity, to cocoa futures.
Cocoa has risen by 15 percent since early this month to one-year high on encouraging technical picture and concerns over longer-term weather-related supply situation.
LIFFE's September coffee fell to a low of $1,790 a tonne before recovering to end $30 lower at $1,815. July was also $28 easier at $1,795.
Switches were again active, partly reflecting concerns over the high failure rate for coffee that are graded in London.
July/Sept and Sept/Nov switches were traded at $15-$20 and Nov/Jan $34.
So far this month, only 27 percent passed the grading and traders attributed this to the new grading rules implemented from the July contract onwards.
